advancement.create_engines.alive.desc: Get an engine running on its own power.
advancement.create_engines.alternator.de: Craft an Alternator to put charge back into a battery from a turning shaft.
advancement.create_engines.battery.desc: Craft a Battery, which supplies the sparks.
advancement.create_engines.big_boost.des: Spool a turbocharger up to a full bar of boost.
advancement.create_engines.blow_off.desc: Dump a turbocharger's boost with a redstone signal.
advancement.create_engines.boost.desc: Spool a turbocharger up to 0.3 bar of boost.
advancement.create_engines.camshaft.desc: Craft a Camshaft. Geared to half the crank's speed, its lobes open the valves on time.
advancement.create_engines.charged_batte: Fill a battery with an alternator.
advancement.create_engines.coupled_crank: Run an engine of four or more cylinders whose crankshafts are geared together one to one, so they turn as one.
advancement.create_engines.cranking.desc: Crank an engine with a starter.
advancement.create_engines.crankshaft.de: Craft a Crankshaft, the spine every engine is built on.
advancement.create_engines.cylinder.desc: Craft a Cylinder, then add a piston and connecting rod.
advancement.create_engines.cylinder_head: Craft a Cylinder Head to seal the bore and hold the injector.
advancement.create_engines.dialed_in.des: Run an engine above 100 RPM with every firing cylinder on a balanced air-fuel mixture.
advancement.create_engines.diesel.desc: Get a bucket of Diesel, which lights readily under compression.
advancement.create_engines.dry_run.desc: Run an engine with no oil in it. It drags terribly, but it runs.
advancement.create_engines.eight_cylinde: Run an engine with eight firing cylinders.
advancement.create_engines.engine_oil.de: Get a bucket of Engine Oil to lubricate the moving parts.
advancement.create_engines.engineer.desc: Burn something on purpose and put the torque to work.
advancement.create_engines.even_firing.d: Run an engine of four or more cylinders whose firings are spaced evenly round the cycle.
advancement.create_engines.every_gear.de: Shift a loaded transmission through all four gears and reverse.
advancement.create_engines.forged_piston: Craft a Forged Piston: lighter and slipperier than a cast one.
advancement.create_engines.fouled_plug.d: Run a spark engine so rich that soot builds up on its plug.
advancement.create_engines.four_cylinder: Run an engine with four firing cylinders.
advancement.create_engines.gasoline.desc: Get a bucket of Gasoline. It will not light by compression, so it needs a spark.
advancement.create_engines.governed.desc: Let a Governor hold a loaded engine on its setting for ten seconds.
advancement.create_engines.governor.desc: Craft a Governor, which moves the fuel rack to hold an engine at a set speed.
advancement.create_engines.heavy_duty.de: Run an engine rated for 16384 stress units or more: as much as a Create steam engine.
advancement.create_engines.high_revs.des: Turn a running engine faster than 200 RPM.
advancement.create_engines.lambda_lock.d: Run an engine above 100 RPM on a balanced mixture with a Lambda Sensor in its exhaust.
advancement.create_engines.lambda_sensor: Craft a Lambda Sensor, which reads the mixture the exhaust gas says was burned.
advancement.create_engines.maf_sensor.de: Craft a MAF Sensor. In an intake run it caps every shot at the air the cylinder drew in.
advancement.create_engines.maf_trim.desc: Run an engine whose MAF sensor is holding every shot back by a fifth or more to match the air.
advancement.create_engines.overloaded.de: Ask an engine for more torque than it is rated for.
advancement.create_engines.pipework.desc: Craft an Intake Manifold: an engine needs air in and exhaust out.
advancement.create_engines.precision_cyl: Craft a Precision Cylinder: a machined liner gives higher compression and less friction.
advancement.create_engines.precision_eng: Run an engine of four or more cylinders built entirely from precision parts.
advancement.create_engines.precision_hea: Craft a Precision Cylinder Head, which breathes better and lights the charge sooner.
advancement.create_engines.precision_inj: Craft a Precision Injector, which atomises fuel finely so it ignites sooner and burns faster.
advancement.create_engines.pushrod_cam.d: Run an engine whose cam sits beside the cylinder block and works the valves through pushrods.
advancement.create_engines.redline.desc: Turn a running engine faster than 240 RPM, close to the limit Create allows.
advancement.create_engines.rev_limited.d: Rev an engine up to a Rev Limiter's setting and let it cut the fuel.
advancement.create_engines.rev_limiter.d: Craft a Rev Limiter and set a speed an engine will not pass.
advancement.create_engines.reverse.desc: Run a transmission's output backwards in reverse gear.
advancement.create_engines.shifted.desc: Change gear on a transmission that is carrying drive.
advancement.create_engines.sixteen_cylin: Run an engine with sixteen firing cylinders.
advancement.create_engines.smoke_signals: Run so rich that fuel pours out of the exhaust as black smoke.
Run an engine whose fuel is lit by a spark plug.
advancement.create_engines.spark_plug.de: Craft a Spark Plug to light fuel by spark instead of by squeezing.
advancement.create_engines.starter.desc: Craft a Starter to crank an engine over.
Run an engine rated for 65536 stress units or more: four Create steam engines' worth from one crankshaft.
advancement.create_engines.sump.desc: Craft an Oil Sump. Set against a crankshaft or head, it oils the whole engine from one place.
advancement.create_engines.thinned_oil.d: Run rich for so long that unburned fuel thins the engine oil.
advancement.create_engines.throttle.desc: Craft a Throttle Body and let redstone decide how much air the engine gets.
advancement.create_engines.timing_tool.d: Craft a Timing Tool, which sets an engine's throws and cam lobes to the best firing order it can have.
advancement.create_engines.tool_timed.de: Time an engine of four or more cylinders with a Timing Tool so every firing is evenly spaced.
Craft a Transmission, a gearbox with selectable gears.
Craft a Turbocharger. Put it in both the exhaust run and the intake run.
advancement.create_engines.twelve_cylind: Run an engine with twelve firing cylinders.
advancement.create_engines.well_oiled.de: Run an engine with every part fully lubricated.
create_engines.goggles.alternator.idle: Idle: needs a turning shaft and a battery that isn't full
create_engines.goggles.alternator.no_bat: No battery touching it or its engine to charge
create_engines.goggles.battery.flat: Flat: an alternator has to charge it
create_engines.goggles.battery.no_engine: Not touching an engine's crankshaft or cylinder head
create_engines.goggles.cam_ratio.wrong: Must turn at half crank speed
create_engines.goggles.cycle.fouled: Misfire: the plug is fouled with soot and can't light a rich mixture
create_engines.goggles.cycle.fuel_cut: Fuel cut by the rev limiter
create_engines.goggles.cycle.no_air: Misfire: no fresh air in the cylinder
create_engines.goggles.cycle.no_spark: Misfire: no spark from the plug
create_engines.goggles.cycle.too_lean: Misfire: mixture too lean for the spark to light
create_engines.goggles.cycle.too_rich: Misfire: mixture too rich for the spark to light
create_engines.goggles.fault.intake_bloc: Intake has no open air intake
create_engines.goggles.fault.no_battery: Spark plug has no battery touching the engine
create_engines.goggles.fault.no_cam: No cam lobe touching the head or the cylinder
create_engines.goggles.fault.not_on_thro: Not mounted on a crank throw
create_engines.goggles.fouling.hint: Caused by running rich. Lean the injector until the mixture burns clean and the plug cleans itself
create_engines.goggles.governor.hint: Fuel (or throttle, in a spark engine) is cut as the engine passes the setting and opened as it falls, over about %1$s%% of the speed. The lowest setting on an engine governs
create_engines.goggles.governor.no_engin: Not touching a crankshaft block or a cylinder head
create_engines.goggles.governor.open: Rack wide open: the load is more than the engine can hold at this speed
create_engines.goggles.head: Cylinder Head
create_engines.goggles.head.metering.hin: Too much fuel runs rich and wastes it, too little runs lean. Breathing falls as the engine speeds up
create_engines.goggles.head.no_injector: Right-click with a Fuel Injector to install
create_engines.goggles.head.no_spark_plu: Right-click with a Spark Plug to light fuel by spark instead of compression
create_engines.goggles.head.oil: Takes Engine Oil as well as fuel: it lubricates the whole engine. An Oil Sump does the same without using a face
create_engines.goggles.lambda.hint: Reads the mixture the exhaust gas says was burned. The redstone output is 8 for balanced, 6 to 9 across the balanced band, lower for lean and higher for rich. It changes nothing itself: feed it to a comparator and the fuel rack on a camshaft for a loop of your own
create_engines.goggles.lambda.none: Nothing has fired on this exhaust to read
create_engines.goggles.limiter.cutting: Cutting fuel: the engine is at its limit
create_engines.goggles.limiter.hint: Holds every injector shut once the crank reaches the limit, and lets fuel back in at %1$s%% of it. The redstone output is how close the engine is to the limit, 15 at it
create_engines.goggles.limiter.no_engine: Not touching a crankshaft block or a cylinder head
create_engines.goggles.lubrication.dry: Dry parts drag: pipe Engine Oil into a cylinder head
create_engines.goggles.lubrication.thinn: Fuel the air can't burn washes into the oil, however much is supplied. It drags the engine until the mixture burns clean
create_engines.goggles.maf.charge: Air charge: %1$s%% of a full breath
create_engines.goggles.maf.cutting: Cutting each shot by %1$s%% to match the air
create_engines.goggles.maf.hint: Caps each injector's shot at the air its cylinder drew in, so Fuel Metering can be set high for slow running and the sensor trims it back as the engine speeds up. It only cuts, never adds. The redstone output is the size of the breath, 15 for one half as large again as the bore
create_engines.goggles.maf.target: Holding the mixture to: %1$s%% of balanced
create_engines.goggles.maf.within: Every shot is within what the air can burn: no fuel cut
create_engines.goggles.phase: Top dead centre at crank angle %1$s°
create_engines.goggles.sensor.no_engine: Not in the intake or exhaust of a running engine's cylinders
create_engines.goggles.starter.idle: Idle: needs a redstone signal and input rotation
create_engines.goggles.state.coasting: Coasting: turning, but nothing is firing
create_engines.goggles.state.overloaded: Overloaded: load is more than its rated torque
create_engines.goggles.sump.empty: Empty: fill it with Engine Oil by bucket or pipe
create_engines.goggles.sump.no_engine: Not touching an engine's crankshaft or cylinder head
create_engines.goggles.throttle.hint: Redstone opens it from its idle stop to wide open. Less air means less power, and its linkage trims the injectors' fuel to match
create_engines.goggles.transmission.gear: Gear %1$s: %2$s turns of the input to one of the output
create_engines.goggles.transmission.hint: The panel sets the gear. A redstone signal picks one instead: 1 neutral, 2 to 5 first to fourth, 6 reverse. A low gear lets the engine carry a heavier load at a slower output
create_engines.goggles.transmission.neut: Neutral: no drive reaches the output
create_engines.goggles.transmission.reve: Reverse: %1$s turns of the input to one of the output, backwards
create_engines.goggles.turbo.hint: Driven by the heat of the exhaust, so it lags and fades with the fuel. Boost packs in more air, which needs more fuel metering to use, and heats the charge. Redstone opens the wastegate fully
create_engines.goggles.turbo.no_compress: Compressor is not on an engine's intake: nothing is boosted
create_engines.goggles.turbo.no_engine: Not on an engine's intake or exhaust
create_engines.goggles.turbo.no_turbine: Turbine is not on an engine's exhaust: nothing drives it
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_1: Every cylinder head needs an intake and an exhaust on its free faces.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_2: Intake Manifolds are pipes. They connect to the heads, pipes and openings beside them, and run from the heads to an Air Intake.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_3: Exhaust Manifolds do the same for an Exhaust Outlet, as pipes can bend and join like a real exhaust. Each opening comfortably serves two cylinders.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_4: A Wrench cuts or restores the pipe connection on the side you click, so two runs can lie side by side without joining.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_5: Openings need a clear mouth. Covering the air intake starves every cylinder on it; an engine that cannot exhaust chokes on its own burned gas.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_6: Smoke from the outlet follows each firing. Black smoke means more fuel than air: the engine is running rich. Turn down the Fuel Metering on its cylinder heads.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_1: A Cam Lobe touching a cylinder head, or the cylinder block below it, opens its valves and fires its injector as the camshaft turns.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_2: In a four-stroke engine the camshaft must turn at exactly half crank speed. Gear it from the crank, for example with a small cogwheel driving a large one.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_3: The Lobe Angle, set with the value panel, decides when the valves open compared with the piston. Goggles show if it is on time, early or late.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_4: Two angles 180° apart both work: each picks which crank revolution the cylinder fires on. This is how firing order is set; the next page shows how.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_5: A redstone signal on the camshaft closes the fuel rack. A full-strength signal cuts the fuel and stops the engine.
create_engines.ponder.compact_v.text_1: A V is two banks of cylinders on the same crank throws: here one bank points up and the other north.
create_engines.ponder.compact_v.text_2: Every head needs an intake and an exhaust, and every head shares fuel, so a tight bank soon runs out of free faces for a camshaft as well.
create_engines.ponder.compact_v.text_3: A Cam Lobe works a cylinder from beside its block as well as beside its head, through pushrods. Put each bank's camshaft on the block and the heads keep their faces for pipes.
create_engines.ponder.compact_v.text_4: The two cylinders on one throw reach top dead centre at different angles, so each bank has its own camshaft and lobe angles. Goggles show when a cylinder is on time.
create_engines.ponder.compact_v.text_5: Add a throw with a cylinder on each side for every two cylinders: six throws make a V12.
create_engines.ponder.coupled_cranks.tex: A crankshaft is an engine. A second line of crank blocks beside it is a second engine, however close: each has its own speed and its own firing.
Gear them together one to one and they become one engine, sharing a single set of revs. Any Create gearing does it: cogwheels, chain drives, gearboxes, belts.

Two meshed cogwheels turn the second crank the other way; the engine allows for it. Each throw's angle still sets its own piston's place in the cycle, and the Timing Tool sets the throws and lobes on every line at once.

Fuel, oil, batteries, sensors and every cylinder on either crank belong to the one engine. It is rated and fired as a whole, so wide W, H and X layouts, or more cylinders than one crank can carry, are just more lines.
Only an exact one-to-one ratio couples. Cranks geared two to one, say, stay separate engines feeding one network, and the faster one wins. Goggles show how many crankshafts an engine has.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_1: A crankshaft is a line of Crankshaft and Crank Throw blocks on one axis. It turns like any Create shaft.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_2: Crank Throws carry an offset crank pin. Cylinders mount on any of their four sides.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_3: Each piston reaches the top of its stroke when the crank pin points up its bore.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_4: A throw's angle can be changed with its value panel. Here the second throw is turned 180°, so its piston moves opposite the first.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_5: Cylinders on different faces of one throw share its pin. This makes a V layout: you never pick an engine type, you build it.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_6: One crankshaft is one engine. It drives the kinetic network through the shafts and gears at its ends.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_1: A Cylinder sits on a Crank Throw, its bore pointing away from the crank.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_2: Install a Connecting Rod and an Engine Piston by right-clicking. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to take them out.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_3: A Cylinder Head closes the bore. It holds the valves and a Fuel Injector, which must be installed.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_4: The head's other faces are its connections: an intake and an exhaust. A Cam Lobe touching the head, or the cylinder below it, works the valves and injector.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_5: Fuel is piped into any face of a head. Every head on the crankshaft shares its fuel, so one pipe can feed the whole engine.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_6: Engine Oil goes in the same way, into a second tank beside the fuel. It lubricates every moving part of the engine, not just this cylinder.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_7: Goggles on any engine part show whether that cylinder is firing, and if not, why.
create_engines.ponder.firing_order.text_: Four cylinders on one crank. Each cam lobe times its cylinder to its own piston, so every one fires. When it fires is set by the lobe angles.
Cylinders 1 and 4 reach top dead centre together, and so do 2 and 3. Timed this simply they fire in pairs: two kicks in two turns, and a lumpy engine.
A lobe angle 180° further round times a cylinder just as well, but fires it on the next crank turn instead. Cylinders 3 and 4 are moved on to the second turn.
Now they fire one after another in the order 1, 3, 4, 2, a power stroke every 180°. Goggles on the crankshaft show the firing intervals.

To plan one by hand: read each piston's top dead centre angle from goggles, halve it for the lobe angle, then add 180° to some lobes so the firings land 720° ÷ cylinders apart. A Timing Tool does all of this for you.
create_engines.ponder.governor.header: Holding an Engine at a Speed
create_engines.ponder.governor.text_1: An engine's speed depends on its load: let go of it and it races, load it and it lugs down. Everything it drives runs at whatever pace that happens to be.
create_engines.ponder.governor.text_2: A Governor set against a crankshaft block or a cylinder head moves the fuel rack to hold the crank at a set speed: it eases the fuel off as the engine speeds up and opens it as it slows.
create_engines.ponder.governor.text_3: Its Governed Speed is set with the value panel, in steps of 5 RPM. A spark engine is governed on its throttle instead, because a charge that is too lean will not light.
create_engines.ponder.governor.text_4: It holds the speed with the torque in hand, so the engine's rating is untouched. If the load is more than the engine can carry at that speed, the rack stays wide open and the engine slows.
create_engines.ponder.governor.text_5: Its redstone output is how far open the rack is held, 15 wide open and 0 shut, so it reads as a load meter. Fit a Rev Limiter as well to stop a runaway.
create_engines.ponder.lambda_sensor.head: Reading the Exhaust with a Lambda Sensor
create_engines.ponder.lambda_sensor.text: A Lambda Sensor is a length of exhaust pipe that reads the mixture the cylinders feeding it burned, from what the exhaust gas still holds.
Its redstone output is the mixture: 8 for balanced, 6 to 9 across the balanced band, lower for lean, higher for rich, and 15 at twice the fuel the air could burn.
It changes nothing by itself. Feed it through a comparator to a camshaft's fuel rack, where redstone closes the rack, and rich running cuts its own fuel.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_1: Crankshaft bearings, pistons and connecting rods all rub against something. They need a film of oil to slide.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_2: A new engine is dry. Dry parts drag: an engine with no oil still runs, but tops out at about half its speed and has less torque to spare.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_3: Pipe Engine Oil into any face of a Cylinder Head. It has a second tank for oil, apart from the fuel. Every head on the crankshaft shares it.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_4: Once oil reaches the engine, the film builds within seconds and friction drops. The engine can turn faster and has more torque to spare.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_5: Turning wears the oil off a little at a time. If the supply runs dry the film thins and the engine slows, so keep the tank topped up.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_6: Goggles on any crankshaft block show how well the engine is lubricated.
create_engines.ponder.lubrication.text_7: Engine Oil is made by heating Plant Oil with a Slime Ball in a Mechanical Mixer over a Blaze Burner.
create_engines.ponder.maf_sensor.header: Matching Fuel to Air with a MAF Sensor
create_engines.ponder.maf_sensor.text_1: An injector delivers the shot it was set to, however much air the cylinder breathed. Breathing falls as the engine speeds up, so a shot that suits slow running is rich at speed.
create_engines.ponder.maf_sensor.text_2: A MAF Sensor is a length of intake pipe that weighs the air each cylinder behind it breathes.
create_engines.ponder.maf_sensor.text_3: Every injector on its network is capped at the fuel that air can burn. It only ever cuts: Fuel Metering stays the most a cylinder gets, so set it high and the sensor trims the shot back as the engine speeds up.
create_engines.ponder.maf_sensor.text_4: Its Mixture Target, set with the value panel, is how lean or rich it holds the shot: 80% to 125% of balanced.
create_engines.ponder.maf_sensor.text_5: It also puts the size of the breath out as redstone: 15 for a boosted cylinder half again as full as its bore. Goggles show the air charge and how much fuel is being cut.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_1: A Fuel Injector delivers the same shot however much air the cylinder drew in. Fuel Metering sets that shot as a share of the usual one.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_2: Turn the dial on the cylinder head's value panel. Each head has its own.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_3: A cylinder breathes less air the faster it turns, so a setting that is right at one speed is rich above it: fuel wasted, black smoke, less power.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_4: Too little fuel is just as bad. A lean cylinder is weak, and a spark engine cannot light a mixture that is too thin or too rich.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_5: Goggles on a cylinder read its air-fuel mixture. Balanced is the target; 2× rich means twice the fuel the air can burn, and 2× lean means half.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_6: Scale Fuel Metering by the reading. At 2× rich, halve it; at 2× lean, double it. Do it with the engine at the speed and load it will really work at, and check again.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_7: Anything that changes the air changes the mixture. A turbocharger packs in more air, so raise the metering to match. A Throttle Body cuts the air and trims the shot with it.
create_engines.ponder.mixture.text_8: To cut fuel to every injector at once, power the camshaft with redstone. A Throttle Body trims it with the air.
create_engines.ponder.precision_parts.te: A Precision Cylinder has a machined liner. It squeezes the charge harder and rubs less, so each stroke makes more work for the same fuel.
A Precision Cylinder Head has four valves and a pent roof. It breathes about half as freely again, which matters most at speed, and lights the charge sooner.
Two parts are installed like their ordinary versions: a Forged Piston, which is lighter and drags less, and a Precision Injector, which atomises the fuel so it ignites sooner and burns faster.
Each part helps on its own and they add up. A fully precision engine rates well over half as much again as a crude one, and a turbocharger multiplies that. They are made from Precision Mechanisms.
create_engines.ponder.rev_limiter.text_1: A Rev Limiter set against a crankshaft block or a cylinder head holds every injector shut once the engine reaches the speed it is set to.
create_engines.ponder.rev_limiter.text_2: Its Rev Limit is set with the value panel, in steps of 5 RPM. Fuel returns a few percent below the limit, so the engine bounces off it instead of revving on.
create_engines.ponder.rev_limiter.text_3: Its redstone output is how near the engine is to its limit, 15 at it: a tachometer. A cylinder that was cut reads "Fuel cut by the rev limiter" in goggles, not a fault.
create_engines.ponder.spark.text_1: A Spark Plug installed in a Cylinder Head lights the fuel with a spark, instead of waiting for compression to heat it. Gasoline is too hard to light by compression alone, so it needs one.
create_engines.ponder.spark.text_2: Plugs fire from a Battery touching the crankshaft or a cylinder head. Each spark uses a little charge, and a flat battery gives no spark.
create_engines.ponder.spark.text_3: A battery makes no charge itself. An Alternator charges the batteries touching it, and those of the engine it touches, while its shaft turns, for a little stress.
create_engines.ponder.spark.text_4: On the crank's own shaft line, cranking charges the battery and the running engine keeps it topped up.
create_engines.ponder.spark.text_5: Each head's injector is metered by hand. A cylinder breathes less air as it speeds up, so a setting that is right at one speed is rich above it: fuel wasted, black smoke, less power. Too little runs lean.
create_engines.ponder.spark.text_6: A spark can only light a mixture that is neither too lean nor too rich. Tune Fuel Metering to the speed the engine runs at, reading each cylinder's mixture through goggles.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_1: A Starter cranks the crankshaft block it faces. It is not connected to the engine's own kinetic network.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_2: Feed it rotation through its back from any source. It cranks the engine at the speed it is turned.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_3: It engages while powered by redstone. Turning a dead engine over takes effort, which appears as stress on the starter's input.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_4: Once the engine fires and runs faster than the starter, a one-way clutch lets go. Remove the signal and it carries on by itself.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_5: A Hand Crank on the crankshaft also works for small engines. Bigger engines need stronger starters.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_1: Engine oil lubricates the whole engine, not one cylinder, so it needs only one place to come in. A head's faces are better spent on intake, exhaust and fuel.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_2: An Oil Sump set against any crankshaft block or cylinder head is the engine's oil pan. It holds a litre of oil, and the engine draws on it as it turns.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_3: Fill it by hand with a bucket of Engine Oil. The film builds within seconds and friction drops.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_4: Or pipe oil into any of its faces from a tank. Pipes carry one fluid at a time, so a sump takes the oil line and the head keeps its fuel line.
create_engines.ponder.sump.text_5: Cylinder heads still take oil too, and the sump is drawn on first. Goggles on the sump show what is left.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_1: A Throttle Body is a length of intake pipe with a valve in it. Close it and every cylinder behind it draws less air.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_2: Its Idle Stop, set with the value panel, is how far open the valve rests with no signal.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_3: Redstone opens it, evenly from the idle stop at no signal to wide open at full strength. A lever, comparator or pedal works like a gas pedal.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_4: Less air means less power: a throttled engine runs slower and has less torque to spare. Nearly shut, the piston spends more dragging air through the valve than it earns.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_5: Its linkage trims every injector's fuel along with the air, so closing it does not flood the engine. Fuel Metering is still tuned for the speed the engine runs at.
create_engines.ponder.throttle.text_6: Throttle bodies in one intake line act together: the most closed one governs every cylinder behind it.
create_engines.ponder.timing_tool.text_1: Set by hand, every crank throw and every cam lobe is a value to work out. Built like this, the cylinders fire in pairs and the engine is lumpy.
create_engines.ponder.timing_tool.text_2: Use a Timing Tool on any block of the engine. It works out the most even firing the layout allows and sets every throw and lobe to it, then tells you the firing order.
create_engines.ponder.timing_tool.text_3: Sneak-use it to change what it may set: any throw angle (smooth), quarter turns (cross-plane V8), half turns (flat-plane), or cams only, which leaves the crank as built and just times the lobes.
create_engines.ponder.timing_tool.text_4: Some layouts can't fire evenly, such as a 90° V12, and a cam lobe shared by two cylinders can only time one of them. The tool says so, and gets as close as it can.
create_engines.ponder.transmission.text_: A Transmission is a gearbox with selectable gears. Rotation goes in at one end of its shaft and comes out of the other at the speed of the gear it is in.
In first gear the output turns four times slower than the input. A load behind it asks the engine for a quarter of the torque it would direct, so an engine can carry a heavier load, slowly.
The value panel picks the gear. Third turns the output at five eighths of the input...
...and fourth drives it direct. Faster output, but the load asks the crank for its full torque.
Neutral lets nothing through, so an engine can start with no load on it.
Reverse turns the output slowly the other way.
A redstone signal picks the gear instead of the panel: strength 1 is neutral, 2 to 5 are first to fourth, and 6 or more is reverse. Shifting briefly cuts the output off.
create_engines.ponder.turbocharger.text_: A Turbocharger sits in the exhaust line and the intake line at once. Exhaust spins its turbine, and the compressor on the shaft's other end pushes air into the engine.
Exhaust pipes join its turbine face and its sides. Here the head's exhaust blows straight into the turbine, and an Exhaust Outlet carries it away.
Intake pipes join its compressor face and its sides. Air comes in at the front and leaves by a pipe to the head, so every cylinder on that line is boosted.
It runs on the heat of the exhaust, so it spools up a moment after the engine fires and fades if the fuel stops. Goggles show its boost and wheel speed.
More air only helps if there is fuel for it. Turn the head's Fuel Metering up to burn it; left alone, the same shot just runs leaner.
Squeezing air heats it, and the turbine holds the exhaust up, so the cylinders push against back-pressure. Under hard boost a spark engine's gasoline can light before the spark.
Its wastegate vents exhaust round the turbine to hold the boost at the limit set on its value panel.
A redstone signal on the turbocharger opens the wastegate fully and dumps the boost, like a blow-off valve.
create_engines.tool.timing_tool.hint: Use on an engine to set its throws and cam lobes. Sneak-use to change what it may set
create_engines.tool.timing_tool.no_cylin: No working cylinder with a cam lobe to time
create_engines.tool.timing_tool.shared: %1$s cylinder(s) share a cam lobe with another that fires at a different time. Give each its own lobe, or move the lobe beside the block
create_engines.tool.timing_tool.skipped: %1$s cylinder(s) were left alone: broken, or with no cam lobe
create_engines.tool.timing_tool.uneven: Timed %1$s cylinders. This layout can't fire evenly; gaps of %2$s: %3$s
